viniyoga: Om. Of this mantra, the Śrī Āditya Hṛdaya hymn, the seer is the sage Śrī Agastya. The metre is anuṣṭubh. The deity is the Lord Brahmā, who is the Āditya Hṛdaya itself. The seed is Om. The word “raśmimate” is its power. The Gāyatrī beginning “tat savituḥ” is its kīlaka (the pin that holds the mantra fast). With every obstacle removed, it is applied in recitation for attaining the knowledge of Brahman and for victory everywhere.
rishyadi: Om, salutation to the sage Agastya: on the head. Salutation to the anuṣṭubh metre: on the mouth. Salutation to the deity Brahmā, who is the Āditya Hṛdaya: on the heart. Om, salutation to the seed: on the private parts. Om, salutation to the power, “raśmimate”: on the feet. Om, salutation to the kīlaka, the Gāyatrī beginning “tat savituḥ”: on the navel. Salutation to the viniyoga: on the whole body.
kara: Om, salutation to the Sun who has rays: on the two thumbs. Om, salutation to the Sun rising in full: on the two forefingers. Om, salutation to the Sun whom gods and asuras salute: on the two middle fingers. Om, salutation to Vivasvān: on the two ring fingers. Om, salutation to Bhāskara: on the two little fingers. Om, salutation to the lord of the worlds: on the palms and the backs of the hands.
anga: Om, to the Sun who has rays: to the heart, salutation. Om, to the Sun rising in full: to the head, svāhā. Om, to the Sun whom gods and asuras salute: to the tuft of hair on the crown, vaṣaṭ. Om, to Vivasvān: to the armour, hum. Om, to Bhāskara: to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ. Om, to the lord of the worlds: to the weapon, phaṭ.
sh1: Then, seeing Śrī Rāma worn out by the fight and standing lost in anxious thought on the battlefield, and Rāvaṇa in front of him, come and standing ready for battle, ॥1॥
sh2: the revered sage Agastya, who had come with the gods to see the battle, went up to Śrī Rāma and said: ॥2॥
sh3: Rāma, mighty-armed Rāma, listen to this eternal secret, dear one, by which you will conquer all your enemies in battle. ॥3॥
sh4: This Āditya Hṛdaya is holy and destroys all enemies; it brings victory and should be recited always; it is imperishable, supreme and auspicious. ॥4॥
sh5: It is the blessing of all blessings and destroys all sins; it calms anxiety and grief, lengthens life and is excellent. ॥5॥
sh6: Worship the Sun, possessed of rays, rising in full, saluted by gods and asuras, Vivasvān, Bhāskara, the lord of the worlds. ॥6॥
sh7: He indeed is the self of all the gods; he is radiant and sustains all by his rays. With his rays he protects the hosts of gods and asuras and the worlds. ॥7॥
sh8: He is Brahmā and Viṣṇu, Śiva, Skanda and Prajāpati; he is Mahendra, Kubera, Kāla, Yama, Soma and Varuṇa, the lord of the waters. ॥8॥
sh9: He is the Pitṛs, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts and Manu; he is Vāyu and Agni, the life-breath of all creatures, the maker of the seasons, the maker of light. ॥9॥
sh10: He is Āditya, Savitṛ, Sūrya, who moves through the sky, Pūṣan, possessed of rays, golden, Bhānu, whose seed is gold, the maker of the day. ॥10॥
sh11: He has green horses, a thousand rays, seven horses, and is full of rays; he churns away the darkness; he is Śambhu, the giver of good, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mārtaṇḍa and Aṃśumān. ॥11॥
sh12: He is Hiraṇyagarbha, the cool one, the one who heats, Bhāskara and Ravi; he holds fire within him; he is the son of Aditi, Śaṅkha the bringer of good, the destroyer of cold. ॥12॥
sh13: He is the lord of the sky, who pierces the darkness, the master of the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas, who sends heavy rain, the friend of the waters, who speeds along the path of the Vindhya. ॥13॥
sh14: He gives the heat of sunshine; his form is a disc; he is death; he is tawny and heats all; he is the all-knowing seer, the universe, of great brilliance, red, the source of all that comes to be. ॥14॥
sh15: He is the lord of the asterisms, the planets and the stars, who brings the universe into being, brilliant even among the brilliant. O you of twelve forms, salutation to you. ॥15॥
sh16: Salutation to the eastern mountain, salutation to the western mountain; salutation to the lord of the hosts of lights, to the lord of the day. ॥16॥
sh17: To the one who is victory, to the good that victory brings, to the one with green horses: salutation, salutation. Salutation, salutation, O thousand-rayed one; to Āditya, salutation, salutation. ॥17॥
sh18: To the fierce one, to the hero, to Sāraṅga, the many-hued: salutation, salutation. Salutation to the one who wakes the lotuses; to Mārtaṇḍa, salutation, salutation. ॥18॥
sh19: To the lord of Brahmā, Śiva and Viṣṇu, to Sūrya, who has the radiance of Āditya, to the shining one, the devourer of all, whose form is fierce like Rudra: salutation. ॥19॥
sh20: To the slayer of darkness, the slayer of cold, the slayer of enemies, whose self is boundless, the destroyer of the ungrateful, the god, the lord of the lights: salutation. ॥20॥
sh21: To the one who shines like molten gold, to the fire, to the maker of the universe, salutation to the one who strikes down the darkness, who is light, the witness of the worlds. ॥21॥
sh22: This Lord destroys the beings, and he creates them again; with his rays he dries, he heats and he rains. ॥22॥
sh23: Firmly abiding within the beings, he stays awake while they sleep; he is the agnihotra, the fire offering, and he is also the fruit of those who keep it. ॥23॥
sh24: He is the Vedas, the sacrifices and the fruit of the sacrifices; of all the deeds done in the worlds, this Sun is the lord. ॥24॥
sh25: Rāghava, in calamities, in hardships, in wild forests and in times of fear, anyone who praises him does not sink in despair. ॥25॥
sh26: With a single-pointed mind, worship him, the god of gods, the lord of the world. Reciting this three times, you will win in battles. ॥26॥
sh27: Mighty-armed one, at this very moment you will slay Rāvaṇa. Having spoken thus, Agastya then went away as he had come. ॥27॥
sh28: Hearing this, Śrī Rāma, of great brilliance, was then freed of his sorrow. Well pleased, his mind controlled and pure, he held it in his mind. ॥28॥
sh29: Looking at the Sun and reciting it, he attained the highest joy. Sipping water three times and becoming pure, the valiant one took up his bow. ॥29॥
sh30: Seeing Rāvaṇa, glad at heart, he came forward to battle, and with all his great effort he resolved on slaying him. ॥30॥
sh31: Then the Sun looked at Śrī Rāma and, glad in mind and rejoicing greatly, knowing that the end of Rāvaṇa, the lord of the demons, was near, standing among the hosts of the gods, he said: Make haste. ॥31॥
iti: Thus ends the hundred and fifth sarga of the Yuddha-kāṇḍa of the holy Rāmāyaṇa, the first poem, composed by the seer Vālmīki.
